Each entry now has 4 examples: two plain, one Konjunktiv II (daily usage), one passive voice — added in a follow-up pass, also authored directly, unreviewed.

entries.intro: The informal second-person singular pronoun — 'you' when speaking to one person you know well (family, friends, children, or by mutual agreement). Its formal counterpart is 'Sie'.
entries.usage: Declines by case: du (nominative), dich (accusative), dir (dative), dein (possessive). Verbs take the '-st' ending with du: du gehst, du bist.

examples.translation: How are you?
Are you coming along?

examples.sentence: Du würdest das bestimmt gut machen.
examples.translation: You would surely do that well.
You are being picked up tonight.

entries.intro: The accusative and dative form of 'ihr' — 'you' (plural, informal), used when addressing more than one person you'd individually call 'du'.
entries.usage: Same form for both accusative and dative: 'Ich sehe euch' (I see you-all) vs. 'Ich gebe euch das Buch' (I give you-all the book).

examples.translation: I missed you (all).
That belongs to you (all).
I would like to invite you all.
You all will be answered soon.

entries.intro: The first-person singular pronoun — 'I'. Always capitalized only at the start of a sentence, unlike English where 'I' is always capitalized.
entries.usage: Declines as: ich (nominative), mich (accusative), mir (dative), mein (possessive).

examples.translation: My name is Anna.
I am hungry.
I would like to try that.
I'm having surgery tomorrow.

entries.intro: The definite article 'the' for neuter nouns, or a demonstrative/relative pronoun meaning 'that/this/which'. Extremely common — it also appears as the all-purpose 'das ist...' ('that is...').
entries.usage: As an article: das Kind (the child), das Haus (the house). As a pronoun: 'Das ist mein Buch' (That is my book).

examples.translation: The house is big.
That was a good movie.
That would be a good idea.
That is currently being investigated.

entries.intro: The definite article 'the' for masculine nominative nouns (and dative/genitive feminine), one of the most frequent words in German. Also functions as a relative pronoun ('who/that').
entries.usage: Declines heavily by case and gender across the der/die/das system — der Mann (the man, nominative masc.) vs. dem Mann (dative masc.).

examples.translation: The man is reading a book.

examples.sentence: Das ist der Mann, der mir geholfen hat.
examples.translation: That's the man who helped me.

examples.sentence: Der Kaffee wäre kalt, wenn wir noch warten.
examples.translation: The coffee would be cold if we waited any longer.
The contract is being signed today.

entries.intro: The definite article 'the' for feminine nominative/accusative nouns, and for all plural nouns regardless of gender. One of the highest-frequency words in the language.
entries.usage: die Frau (the woman, singular feminine), die Kinder (the children, plural — any gender).

examples.translation: The woman works at the hospital.

examples.sentence: Die Bücher liegen auf dem Tisch.
examples.translation: The books are lying on the table.

examples.sentence: Die Reise wäre teurer im Sommer.
examples.translation: The trip would be more expensive in summer.

examples.sentence: Die Rechnung wird per E-Mail geschickt.
examples.translation: The invoice is sent by email.

entries.intro: A two-way preposition meaning 'at' or 'on' (vertical surfaces, edges, points in time) — takes accusative for motion toward, dative for static location.
entries.usage: an + dative = location ('am Fenster' — at the window); an + accusative = direction ('an die Wand' — onto the wall).

examples.sentence: Das Bild hängt an der Wand.
examples.translation: The picture is hanging on the wall.
We're meeting on Monday.

examples.sentence: Ich würde gern an dich denken.
examples.translation: I would like to think of you.

examples.sentence: An der Grenze wird der Ausweis kontrolliert.
examples.translation: At the border, the ID is checked.

entries.intro: A two-way preposition meaning 'on/onto/upon' (horizontal surfaces) — dative for location, accusative for motion onto something.
entries.usage: auf + dative = 'auf dem Tisch' (on the table, static); auf + accusative = 'auf den Tisch' (onto the table, motion).

examples.sentence: Das Buch liegt auf dem Tisch.
examples.translation: The book is lying on the table.

examples.sentence: Leg das Buch auf den Tisch.
examples.translation: Put the book on the table.

examples.sentence: Ich würde mich auf dich verlassen.
examples.translation: I would rely on you.

examples.sentence: Auf der Baustelle wird viel Lärm gemacht.
examples.translation: A lot of noise is made at the construction site.

entries.intro: A preposition meaning 'after' (time/sequence) or 'to/toward' (with city and country names, and cardinal directions). Always takes the dative case.
entries.usage: nach + dative always: 'nach der Arbeit' (after work), 'nach Berlin' (to Berlin).

examples.translation: We're going to Berlin.

examples.sentence: Nach dem Essen gehen wir spazieren.
examples.translation: After eating, we go for a walk.

examples.sentence: Ich würde gern nach Hause fahren.
examples.translation: I would like to drive home.

examples.sentence: Nach der Arbeit wird das Büro abgeschlossen.
examples.translation: After work, the office is locked up.

entries.intro: The indefinite article 'a/an' for masculine and neuter nominative nouns. Also used as the numeral 'one' in some contexts.
entries.usage: ein Mann (a man, masc.), ein Kind (a child, neut.) — declines to einen/einem/eines by case.

examples.translation: I have a car.
That's a good plan.
A vacation would be perfect right now.
A mistake was quickly corrected.

entries.intro: The neuter third-person singular pronoun 'it', and also the impersonal subject used in weather/time expressions and many fixed phrases ('es gibt' — there is/are).
entries.usage: Refers back to neuter nouns, and appears as a placeholder subject: 'Es regnet' (It's raining).

examples.translation: It's raining today.
There are many possibilities.

examples.sentence: Es wäre schade, das zu verpassen.
examples.translation: It would be a shame to miss that.
It is not told to anyone.

entries.intro: Used in the fixed pair 'sowohl ... als auch' ('both ... and', literally 'as well ... as also') to link two items that are both true or included.
entries.usage: Always paired with 'als auch': 'sowohl A als auch B'.

examples.sentence: Sie spricht sowohl Deutsch als auch Englisch.
examples.translation: She speaks both German and English.

examples.sentence: Er mag sowohl Kaffee als auch Tee.
examples.translation: He likes both coffee and tea.

examples.sentence: Man könnte sowohl das eine als auch das andere wählen.
examples.translation: One could choose both.

examples.sentence: Sowohl der Text als auch die Bilder wurden überarbeitet.
examples.translation: Both the text and the images were revised.

entries.intro: The basic coordinating conjunction 'and', linking words, phrases, or clauses of equal weight. One of the most frequent words in any German text.
entries.usage: Doesn't change word order in the clause that follows it (unlike subordinating conjunctions).

examples.translation: I'm buying bread and milk.

examples.sentence: Er kam nach Hause und schlief sofort ein.
examples.translation: He came home and fell asleep immediately.

examples.sentence: Ich würde bleiben, und du könntest gehen.
examples.translation: I would stay, and you could go.

examples.sentence: Das Zimmer wurde geputzt, und die Betten wurden gemacht.
examples.translation: The room was cleaned, and the beds were made.

entries.intro: As an adverb, 'there/here' (pointing to a place already established). As a subordinating conjunction, 'since/because' (giving a reason, often at the start of a sentence).
entries.usage: As a conjunction it sends the verb to the end of its clause: 'Da es regnet, bleiben wir zu Hause.'

examples.sentence: Da es regnet, bleiben wir zu Hause.
examples.translation: Since it's raining, we're staying home.
Is anyone there?

examples.sentence: Da es spät wäre, würden wir ein Taxi nehmen.
examples.translation: Since it would be late, we would take a taxi.

examples.sentence: Da wird schon seit Stunden gebaut.
examples.translation: It's been under construction there for hours.

entries.intro: 'Former/of that time' — describes something as it was at a specific point in the past being discussed, not now.
entries.usage: Almost always used attributively before a noun: 'der damalige Präsident' (the president at that time).

examples.sentence: Der damalige Bürgermeister traf diese Entscheidung.
examples.translation: The mayor at that time made this decision.

examples.sentence: Das damalige System war viel langsamer.
examples.translation: The system at that time was much slower.

examples.sentence: Die damalige Lösung wäre heute nicht mehr sinnvoll.
examples.translation: The solution at that time wouldn't make sense today.

examples.sentence: Der damalige Fehler wurde später korrigiert.
examples.translation: The mistake made at that time was later corrected.

entries.intro: A preposition meaning 'out of' or 'from' (origin) — always takes the dative case. Also used to describe material something is made of.
entries.usage: aus + dative: 'aus Deutschland' (from Germany), 'aus Holz' (made of wood).

examples.translation: She is from Germany.
The table is made of wood.

examples.sentence: Ich würde gern aus der Stadt wegziehen.
examples.translation: I would like to move away from the city.

examples.sentence: Der Kuchen wird aus frischen Eiern gebacken.
examples.translation: The cake is baked from fresh eggs.

entries.intro: A preposition meaning 'from/of/by' — always dative. Used for origin, possession (informally, instead of the genitive), and the agent in passive sentences.
entries.usage: von + dative: 'von mir' (from me / of mine), 'von dem Lehrer gelobt' (praised by the teacher).

examples.sentence: Das Geschenk ist von meiner Schwester.
examples.translation: The gift is from my sister.

examples.sentence: Das Buch wurde von einem berühmten Autor geschrieben.
examples.translation: The book was written by a famous author.

examples.sentence: Ich würde das gern von dir lernen.
examples.translation: I would like to learn that from you.

examples.sentence: Die Entscheidung wird von der Regierung getroffen.
examples.translation: The decision is made by the government.

entries.intro: A two-way preposition meaning 'before/in front of' (space or time) — dative for location, accusative for motion. Also used with a time expression to mean 'ago'.
entries.usage: vor + dative for static position/time-ago: 'vor dem Haus' (in front of the house), 'vor drei Jahren' (three years ago).

examples.sentence: Das Auto steht vor dem Haus.
examples.translation: The car is parked in front of the house.
That was three years ago.

examples.sentence: Ich hätte Respekt vor so einer Aufgabe.
examples.translation: I would have respect for such a task.

examples.sentence: Vor dem Konzert wird der Saal vorbereitet.
examples.translation: Before the concert, the hall is prepared.

entries.intro: The third-person singular present tense of 'sein' (to be) — 'is'. One of the most irregular and most frequent verbs in German.
entries.usage: sein conjugates irregularly: ich bin, du bist, er/sie/es ist, wir sind, ihr seid, sie sind. Past: war. Perfect: ist gewesen.

examples.translation: She is a doctor.
The weather is nice today.

examples.sentence: Wenn es wahr wäre, wäre das erstaunlich, aber es ist unklar.
examples.translation: If it were true, that would be amazing, but it is unclear.

examples.sentence: Es ist bekannt, dass hier viel gebaut wird.
examples.translation: It is known that a lot is being built here.

entries.intro: 'Into/inward' — describes motion from the speaker's position toward the inside of something, away from the speaker.
entries.usage: Often combines with verbs as a separable prefix: hineingehen (to go in), hineinschauen (to look in).

examples.sentence: Er ging in das dunkle Zimmer hinein.
examples.translation: He went into the dark room.

examples.sentence: Sie schaute neugierig ins Zimmer hinein.
examples.translation: She looked curiously into the room.

examples.sentence: Ich würde gern in den Garten hinein schauen.
examples.translation: I would like to look into the garden.

examples.sentence: Das Licht wird ins Zimmer hinein geleitet.
examples.translation: The light is directed into the room.

entries.intro: The interrogative and relative pronoun 'what' — used to ask questions and to refer back to indefinite pronouns or whole clauses.
entries.usage: As a question word: 'Was machst du?' (What are you doing?). As a relative pronoun: 'Alles, was ich weiß' (Everything that I know).

examples.translation: What would you like to drink?

examples.sentence: Ich weiß nicht, was passiert ist.
examples.translation: I don't know what happened.

examples.sentence: Ich würde gern wissen, was du denkst.
examples.translation: I would like to know what you think.

examples.sentence: Was hier gebaut wird, ist noch geheim.
examples.translation: What is being built here is still secret.

entries.intro: The impersonal pronoun 'one/you/people (in general)' — used to make a generalized statement without naming a specific subject. Very common in spoken and written German where English often uses 'you' or the passive voice.
entries.usage: Only ever used in the nominative case, always with a third-person-singular verb: 'Man sagt...' (People/one say(s)...).

examples.translation: You can eat well here.
One doesn't do that.
One could get that done faster.

examples.sentence: Man wird über die Änderung informiert.
examples.translation: One is informed about the change.

entries.intro: The accusative form of 'ich' — 'me', used as a direct object or after accusative prepositions.
entries.usage: 'Er sieht mich' (He sees me) — contrast with dative 'mir' (to/for me).

examples.translation: Can you hear me?
She invited me.
It would please me a lot.

examples.sentence: Ich wurde gestern gefragt, und das hat mich überrascht.
examples.translation: I was asked yesterday, and that surprised me.

entries.intro: The dative form of 'ich' — 'to me/for me', used as an indirect object and with dative verbs/prepositions.
entries.usage: 'Gib mir das Buch' (Give me the book) — the recipient, not the direct object.

examples.translation: I like that a lot (literally: that pleases me).
Can you help me?
That would help me a lot.
The door was opened for me.

entries.intro: The demonstrative 'this/these' for feminine singular nouns and all plural nouns — points to something specific and nearby (physically or in the conversation).
entries.usage: diese Frau (this woman, fem. sg.), diese Bücher (these books, plural).

examples.translation: I don't know this woman.
These shoes are too small.

examples.sentence: Diese Idee wäre einen Versuch wert.
examples.translation: This idea would be worth a try.
These rules are strictly followed.

entries.intro: The demonstrative 'this' for masculine singular nominative nouns — points to something specific and nearby.
entries.usage: dieser Mann (this man) — declines to diesen/diesem/dieses by case, same pattern as 'der'.

examples.translation: This man helped me.
This chair belongs to me.
This plan would be risky.
This letter was sent yesterday.

entries.intro: The demonstrative 'this' for neuter singular nominative/accusative nouns.
entries.usage: dieses Jahr (this year), dieses Buch (this book).

examples.translation: This year was special.
This car is new.
This result would be unexpected.
This house is being sold soon.

entries.intro: The third-person singular masculine pronoun 'he' (or 'it', when referring back to a masculine noun).
entries.usage: Declines as: er (nominative), ihn (accusative), ihm (dative).

examples.translation: He lives in Munich.

examples.sentence: Wo ist der Schlüssel? Er liegt auf dem Tisch.
examples.translation: Where is the key? It's on the table.
He would surely understand that.
He is having surgery tomorrow.

entries.intro: Has three common uses: 'when' (for a single past event), 'as' (in a role/capacity), and 'than' (in comparisons).
entries.usage: Sends the verb to the end of its clause as a subordinating conjunction: 'Als ich ankam, regnete es.'

examples.sentence: Als ich jung war, wohnte ich in Berlin.
examples.translation: When I was young, I lived in Berlin.
She is taller than me.

examples.sentence: Als Kind hätte ich das nie gewagt.
examples.translation: As a child I would never have dared that.

examples.sentence: Als Erstes wird das Formular ausgefüllt.
examples.translation: First, the form is filled out.

entries.intro: A coordinating conjunction meaning 'because/for', giving a reason — similar meaning to 'weil' but, unlike 'weil', doesn't change the word order of its clause.
entries.usage: Keeps normal (verb-second) word order, unlike 'weil'/'da': 'Ich bleibe zu Hause, denn ich bin müde.'

examples.sentence: Ich bleibe zu Hause, denn ich bin müde.
examples.translation: I'm staying home, because I'm tired.

examples.sentence: Wir feiern, denn heute ist ihr Geburtstag.
examples.translation: We're celebrating, because today is her birthday.

examples.sentence: Ich würde nicht gehen, denn es wäre zu gefährlich.
examples.translation: I wouldn't go, because it would be too dangerous.

examples.sentence: Es wird gefeiert, denn der Vertrag wurde unterschrieben.
examples.translation: There's a celebration, because the contract was signed.

entries.intro: A preposition meaning 'for' — always takes the accusative case. Used for purpose, benefit, duration, or exchange.
entries.usage: für + accusative always: 'für mich' (for me), 'für zwei Wochen' (for two weeks).

examples.translation: The gift is for you.

examples.sentence: Ich brauche das für die Arbeit.
examples.translation: I need that for work.

examples.sentence: Das wäre gut für uns alle.
examples.translation: That would be good for all of us.

examples.sentence: Für das Projekt wird noch Geld gesammelt.
examples.translation: Money is still being collected for the project.

entries.intro: The possessive pronoun 'my', used before masculine/neuter singular nouns (nominative) or as a predicate.
entries.usage: mein Bruder (my brother), meine Schwester (my sister, fem.) — declines like 'ein'.

examples.translation: This is my brother.
My car is broken.
My plan would be to start early.
My application was approved.

entries.intro: A preposition meaning 'at/near/with (someone's place)' — always dative. Common in expressions of location, company, and circumstance.
entries.usage: bei + dative always: 'bei mir' (at my place), 'bei der Arbeit' (while working).

examples.translation: I'm at my girlfriend's place.
If it rains, we'll stay inside.

examples.sentence: Bei schönem Wetter würden wir draußen essen.
examples.translation: In good weather, we would eat outside.

examples.sentence: Bei der Prüfung wird nichts außer einem Stift erlaubt.
examples.translation: At the exam, nothing but a pen is allowed.

entries.intro: The possessive pronoun 'your' (informal singular), the 'du'-form counterpart to 'mein'.
entries.usage: dein Buch (your book), deine Tasche (your bag, fem.) — declines like 'ein'.

examples.translation: Is that your car?
Where is your phone?

examples.sentence: Dein Vorschlag wäre eine gute Lösung.
examples.translation: Your suggestion would be a good solution.
Your package will be delivered tomorrow.

entries.intro: The possessive pronoun 'your' (informal plural), the 'ihr'-form counterpart to 'mein'.
entries.usage: euer Haus (your house), eure Kinder (your children) — note the dropped 'e' when an ending is added: euer → eure, not euere.

examples.translation: Is that your (all's) house?
How was your (all's) vacation?

examples.sentence: Euer Plan wäre einen Versuch wert.
examples.translation: Your (all's) plan would be worth a try.

examples.sentence: Euer Haus wird nächstes Jahr renoviert.
examples.translation: Your (all's) house is being renovated next year.

entries.intro: The simple past (first/third person singular) of 'sein' (to be) — 'was'. German's simple past of 'sein' is used in speech far more than most other verbs' simple past forms.
entries.usage: ich/er/sie/es war, du warst, wir/sie waren, ihr wart.

examples.translation: The weather was bad yesterday.

examples.sentence: Ich war noch nie in Japan.
examples.translation: I've never been to Japan.

examples.sentence: Wäre es nicht so spät gewesen, wären wir noch geblieben.
examples.translation: If it hadn't been so late, we would have stayed.

examples.sentence: Es wurde gesagt, dass die Party gut war.
examples.translation: It was said that the party was good.

entries.intro: The simple past (first/third person singular) of 'werden' — 'became', or the auxiliary used to form the passive voice in the past tense ('was [verb]ed').
entries.usage: As passive auxiliary: 'Das Haus wurde gebaut' (The house was built).

examples.translation: He became a doctor.
The book was published in 1990.

examples.sentence: Es wäre schön gewesen, wenn er eingeladen worden wäre.
examples.translation: It would have been nice if he had been invited.

examples.sentence: Das Museum wurde letztes Jahr eröffnet.
examples.translation: The museum was opened last year.

entries.intro: The negative article 'no/not a/not any' — negates a noun the way 'nicht' negates a verb or adjective. Used instead of 'nicht ein'.
entries.usage: kein Geld (no money), keine Zeit (no time, fem.) — declines like 'ein'.

examples.translation: I have no money.
That's no problem.
I would have no problem with that.
No word was forgotten.

entries.intro: The feminine/plural form of 'kein' — 'no/not any', negating feminine singular or any plural noun.
entries.usage: keine Zeit (no time, fem. sg.), keine Bücher (no books, plural).

examples.translation: I have no time.
We have no children.
I would have no time for that.
No exception is made.

entries.intro: The general-purpose negation word 'not' — negates verbs, adjectives, and whole statements (as opposed to 'kein', which negates nouns).
entries.usage: Typically placed after the verb and direct object, but before what's being negated: 'Ich verstehe das nicht' (I don't understand that).

examples.translation: I don't understand that.
That's not correct.
That wouldn't be necessary.
That is not allowed.

entries.intro: The second-person plural present tense of 'sein' (to be) — 'are' (you all are). Easy to confuse with the possessive 'seid' vs. reflexive 'sich' vs. 'seit' (since) — a very common spelling mix-up even among native speakers.
entries.usage: ihr seid — used only with 'ihr'.

examples.translation: You (all) are my best friends.
Are you (all) ready?
You all would certainly be welcome.

examples.sentence: Ihr seid eingeladen, und die Einladung wird morgen verschickt.
examples.translation: You are invited, and the invitation is being sent tomorrow.

entries.intro: The present tense of 'sein' (to be) used with 'wir', 'sie' (they), and the formal 'Sie' — 'are'.
entries.usage: wir sind, sie sind, Sie sind (formal).

examples.translation: We are finished.
You are (formal)/They are very nice.
We would have liked to be there.

examples.sentence: Die Plätze sind schon reserviert worden.
examples.translation: The seats have already been reserved.

entries.intro: The first- and third-person singular present tense of 'können' (can/to be able to) — one of German's core modal verbs.
entries.usage: ich/er/sie/es kann, du kannst, wir/sie können, ihr könnt. Past: konnte. Perfect: hat gekonnt / hat + infinitive + können.

examples.translation: I can swim well.
Can you help me?

examples.sentence: Ich könnte das machen, wenn ich Zeit hätte.
examples.translation: I could do that if I had time.
It cannot be confirmed.

entries.intro: A preposition meaning 'with' — always dative. Used for accompaniment, means/tools, and manner.
entries.usage: mit + dative always: 'mit mir' (with me), 'mit dem Auto' (by car).

examples.translation: I'm going by car.
Are you coming with me?

examples.sentence: Ich würde gern mit dir reden.
examples.translation: I would like to talk with you.

examples.sentence: Mit großem Interesse wird das Projekt verfolgt.
examples.translation: The project is being followed with great interest.

entries.intro: The most common word for 'but' — introduces a contrast without implying the first statement was wrong (contrast with 'sondern').
entries.usage: Doesn't change word order: 'Ich bin müde, aber ich arbeite weiter.'

examples.sentence: Ich bin müde, aber ich arbeite weiter.
examples.translation: I'm tired, but I'm continuing to work.
He is small, but strong.

examples.sentence: Ich würde kommen, aber ich hätte keine Zeit.
examples.translation: I would come, but I would have no time.

examples.sentence: Das Fenster wurde repariert, aber die Tür wird noch gestrichen.
examples.translation: The window was repaired, but the door is still being painted.

entries.intro: 'But rather' — used after a negated statement to introduce the correct alternative, not just a contrast (unlike 'aber').
entries.usage: Only follows a 'nicht'/'kein' clause: 'Das ist nicht rot, sondern blau.'

examples.sentence: Das ist nicht rot, sondern blau.
examples.translation: That's not red, but rather blue.

examples.sentence: Ich will nicht warten, sondern sofort anfangen.
examples.translation: I don't want to wait, but rather start right away.

examples.sentence: Es wäre nicht schwer, sondern einfach.
examples.translation: It wouldn't be hard, but rather easy.

examples.sentence: Das wird nicht ignoriert, sondern ernst genommen.
examples.translation: That is not ignored, but rather taken seriously.

entries.intro: 'All' — the uninflected/short form used before another determiner: 'all das' (all that), 'all mein Geld' (all my money).
entries.usage: Less common on its own than 'alle'; often precedes another article or possessive.

examples.translation: All that money is gone.
All my friends were there.

examples.sentence: All das Geld wäre schnell ausgegeben.
examples.translation: All that money would be spent quickly.
All of that is still being checked.

entries.intro: 'All/everyone' — the inflected plural form, one of the most common ways to say 'all' or 'everybody' in German.
entries.usage: alle Leute (all people), or standalone: 'Alle sind da' (Everyone is here).

examples.translation: Everyone is invited.
I know everyone here.

examples.sentence: Alle wären froh über eine Pause.
examples.translation: Everyone would be glad about a break.
All questions are answered.

entries.intro: 'Whole/entire' as an adjective, or 'quite/completely' as an intensifying adverb before another adjective.
entries.usage: die ganze Stadt (the whole city); ganz gut (quite good).

examples.sentence: Ich habe die ganze Nacht gearbeitet.
examples.translation: I worked the whole night.
That's quite simple.
That would be quite simple.
The whole apartment is being renovated.

entries.intro: 'So/therefore/thus' — a very common connector introducing a conclusion or a rephrasing, similar in feel to English 'so...' at the start of a sentence.
entries.usage: Triggers verb-second word order: 'Also, ich denke...' (So, I think...).

examples.sentence: Es regnet, also bleibe ich zu Hause.
examples.translation: It's raining, so I'm staying home.
So, let's begin.

examples.sentence: Also, ich würde das anders machen.
examples.translation: So, I would do that differently.
So the meeting is being postponed.

entries.intro: 'Therefore/from there' — introduces a logical consequence, more formal-sounding than 'also'.
entries.usage: Triggers inversion when it starts the clause: 'Daher bleiben wir zu Hause.'

examples.sentence: Es regnet stark, daher bleiben wir zu Hause.
examples.translation: It's raining heavily, therefore we're staying home.

examples.sentence: Sie war krank, daher blieb sie zu Hause.
examples.translation: She was sick, therefore she stayed home.

examples.sentence: Es regnete, daher wären wir sowieso zu Hause geblieben.
examples.translation: It was raining, so we would have stayed home anyway.

examples.sentence: Die Straße ist gesperrt, daher wird ein Umweg empfohlen.
examples.translation: The street is closed, therefore a detour is recommended.

entries.intro: 'So/like this/that' — one of the most versatile German adverbs: used for degree ('so groß' — so big), manner ('mach es so' — do it like this), and as a filler.
entries.usage: Often paired with 'wie' for comparisons: 'so groß wie...' (as big as...).

examples.translation: She is so nice.
Just do it like this.

examples.sentence: Ich würde es nicht so machen.
examples.translation: I wouldn't do it like this.

examples.sentence: So wird das Brot traditionell gebacken.
examples.translation: This is how bread is traditionally baked.

entries.intro: 'Simple/easy' as an adjective, or 'simply/just' as an adverb emphasizing ease or directness.
entries.usage: Das ist einfach (That's simple); Sag es einfach (Just say it).

examples.translation: This task is easy.
Just call me.
That would be simple to solve.
The rules are explained simply.

entries.intro: 'Exact/precise' as an adjective, or 'exactly/precisely' as an adverb — also used alone as an agreement ('Genau!' — 'Exactly!').
entries.usage: genau um drei Uhr (exactly at three o'clock).

examples.sentence: Das ist genau das, was ich wollte.
examples.translation: That's exactly what I wanted.
Exactly!
That would be exactly right.
The numbers are precisely checked.

entries.intro: 'Just (now)/right now' as a temporal adverb, or 'straight' as an adjective (e.g. a straight line).
entries.usage: Ich esse gerade (I'm just now eating); eine gerade Linie (a straight line).

examples.translation: I'm busy right now.
Draw a straight line.

examples.sentence: Jetzt wäre gerade ein guter Zeitpunkt.
examples.translation: Right now would be a good time.
The line is drawn straight.

entries.intro: 'There' — refers to a location away from the speaker, more formal/written than 'da' in this sense.
entries.usage: Static location, contrast with 'dorthin' (motion toward there).

examples.translation: The restaurant is over there.
I saw you there.
It would be quieter there.

examples.sentence: Dort wird ein neues Gebäude errichtet.
examples.translation: A new building is being erected there.

entries.intro: '(To) there' — the directional counterpart of 'dort', indicating motion toward that place.
entries.usage: Contrast with static 'dort': 'Wir fahren dorthin' (We're driving there).

examples.translation: We're going there tomorrow.
The way there is long.
I would like to travel there.
The packages are delivered there.

entries.intro: 'Here' — refers to the speaker's current location.
entries.usage: Static; the directional counterpart is 'hierher' (to here).

examples.translation: I live here.
Come here!
There would be enough room here.

examples.sentence: Hier wird ein neuer Park gebaut.
examples.translation: A new park is being built here.

entries.intro: Covers three distinct meanings depending on capitalization/context: lowercase 'sie' = 'she' or 'they'; capitalized 'Sie' = the formal 'you'.
entries.usage: Verb agreement disambiguates: 'sie ist' (she is) vs. 'sie sind' (they are) vs. 'Sie sind' (you are, formal).

examples.translation: She lives in Hamburg.
They are coming tomorrow.
She would surely manage that.
She is having surgery tomorrow.

entries.intro: 'To like/be fond of' — usually written as two words, 'gern haben', meaning to have affection for someone or something, gentler than 'lieben' (to love).
entries.usage: Conjugates via 'haben': ich habe dich gern (I'm fond of you) — literally 'have gladly'.

examples.translation: I'm very fond of you.

examples.sentence: Kinder haben Tiere oft sehr gern.
examples.translation: Children are often very fond of animals.
I would always be fond of you.

examples.sentence: Es wird oft gesagt, dass man sie sehr gernhat.
examples.translation: It is often said that people are very fond of her.

entries.intro: 'Same/equal' as an adjective, or 'right away/in a moment' as a temporal adverb.
entries.usage: gleiche Größe (same size); Ich komme gleich (I'll be right there).

examples.translation: We have the same opinion.
I'll be done in a moment.
I would be finished shortly.
The tasks are being distributed right now.

entries.intro: 'How' (question word) or 'as/like' (comparison) — extremely common in both questions and comparative constructions.
entries.usage: Wie geht's? (How's it going?); so groß wie du (as tall as you).

examples.translation: What is your name? (literally: How are you called?)
She sings like a professional.

examples.sentence: Ich würde gern wissen, wie das funktioniert.
examples.translation: I would like to know how that works.

examples.sentence: Wie das gemacht wird, ist noch unklar.
examples.translation: How it's done is still unclear.

entries.intro: 'To bring' — to carry or deliver something/someone to a place. An irregular verb.
entries.usage: bringen, brachte, hat gebracht. 'Ich bringe dir das Buch' (I'll bring you the book).

examples.translation: Can you bring me coffee?
Please bring me the salt.

examples.sentence: Ich würde dir das Buch bringen.
examples.translation: I would bring you the book.
The food is being brought shortly.

entries.intro: 'To receive' (formally) or 'to preserve/maintain' — a common verb with two related but distinct senses.
entries.usage: erhalten, erhielt, hat erhalten. 'Ich habe deine Nachricht erhalten' (I received your message).

examples.translation: I received your email.
We must preserve nature.

examples.sentence: Ich würde gern eine Antwort erhalten.
examples.translation: I would like to receive an answer.

examples.sentence: Die Nachricht wurde von allen erhalten.
examples.translation: The message was received by everyone.

entries.intro: 'To fetch/get' — to go and bring something back, often used casually in everyday speech.
entries.usage: holen (regular): holte, hat geholt. 'Ich hole die Post' (I'll get the mail).

examples.translation: I'll quickly get some bread.

examples.sentence: Kannst du die Kinder von der Schule holen?
examples.translation: Can you pick up the kids from school?

examples.sentence: Ich würde dir gern Wasser holen.
examples.translation: I would gladly fetch you water.

examples.sentence: Die Pakete werden vom Boten geholt.
examples.translation: The packages are picked up by the courier.

entries.intro: 'In case/if' — introduces a conditional clause, similar to 'wenn' but with a stronger sense of 'in the event that'.
entries.usage: Sends the verb to the end of its clause: 'Falls es regnet, bleiben wir drinnen.'

examples.sentence: Falls es regnet, bleiben wir drinnen.
examples.translation: In case it rains, we'll stay inside.

examples.sentence: Falls du Hilfe brauchst, ruf mich an.
examples.translation: In case you need help, call me.

examples.sentence: Falls es regnen würde, blieben wir drinnen.
examples.translation: In case it would rain, we would stay inside.

examples.sentence: Falls nötig, wird die Reise verschoben.
examples.translation: If necessary, the trip is postponed.

entries.intro: 'Whether/if' — introduces an indirect yes/no question.
entries.usage: Sends the verb to the end of its clause: 'Ich weiß nicht, ob er kommt.'

examples.sentence: Ich weiß nicht, ob er kommt.
examples.translation: I don't know whether he's coming.

examples.sentence: Sie fragte, ob ich mitkommen möchte.
examples.translation: She asked whether I wanted to come along.

examples.sentence: Ich wüsste gern, ob das stimmen würde.
examples.translation: I would like to know whether that would be true.

examples.sentence: Es wird geprüft, ob alles korrekt ist.
examples.translation: It is checked whether everything is correct.

entries.intro: 'If/whenever' — introduces a conditional or repeated-time clause. The most common way to say 'if' in German.
entries.usage: Sends the verb to the end of its clause: 'Wenn es regnet, bleibe ich zu Hause.'

examples.sentence: Wenn du Zeit hast, ruf mich an.
examples.translation: If you have time, call me.

examples.sentence: Wenn ich müde bin, gehe ich früh ins Bett.
examples.translation: Whenever I'm tired, I go to bed early.

examples.sentence: Wenn ich Zeit hätte, würde ich mehr lesen.
examples.translation: If I had time, I would read more.
If necessary, help is fetched.

entries.intro: 'Out of town/away' — describes being or doing something away from home, or (in sports) an away game.
entries.usage: auswärts essen (to eat out); ein Auswärtsspiel (an away game).

examples.translation: We're eating out today.

examples.sentence: Das Team spielt am Samstag auswärts.
examples.translation: The team plays away on Saturday.
We would rather eat out.
The game is being played away.

entries.intro: 'Outside of' — a genitive preposition describing being outside a boundary, place, or time period.
entries.usage: außerhalb + genitive: 'außerhalb der Stadt' (outside the city).

examples.translation: We live outside the city.

examples.sentence: Der Flughafen liegt außerhalb der Stadt.
examples.translation: The airport is located outside the city.

examples.sentence: Außerhalb der Stadt wäre es ruhiger.
examples.translation: Outside the city it would be quieter.

examples.sentence: Außerhalb der Öffnungszeiten wird niemand bedient.
examples.translation: Outside opening hours, no one is served.

entries.intro: 'To notify/inform' — a somewhat formal verb used to tell someone about something officially or urgently.
entries.usage: benachrichtigen (regular, weak): benachrichtigte, hat benachrichtigt.

examples.sentence: Wir werden Sie benachrichtigen, sobald es fertig ist.
examples.translation: We will notify you as soon as it's ready.

examples.sentence: Bitte benachrichtige mich, wenn du ankommst.
examples.translation: Please notify me when you arrive.
I would notify you immediately.

examples.sentence: Alle Kunden werden per E-Mail benachrichtigt.
examples.translation: All customers are notified by email.

entries.intro: 'Approximately/about' (with numbers), or 'perhaps/by any chance' (softening a question, often suggesting doubt or surprise).
entries.usage: etwa zehn Minuten (about ten minutes); 'Bist du etwa krank?' (Are you sick, by any chance?).

examples.translation: It takes about ten minutes.

examples.sentence: Es waren etwa zwanzig Leute da.
examples.translation: There were about twenty people there.
It would be about five o'clock.
About a hundred guests are expected.

entries.intro: 'Against/toward' — always accusative. Used for opposition (sports, arguments), approximate time, and physical direction.
entries.usage: gegen + accusative always: 'gegen die Wand' (against the wall), 'gegen sechs Uhr' (around six o'clock).

examples.sentence: Wir spielen heute gegen die Bayern.
examples.translation: We're playing against Bayern today.
I'll come around six o'clock.

examples.sentence: Ich hätte nichts gegen einen Kaffee.
examples.translation: I would have nothing against a coffee.
There is protest against the decision.

entries.intro: 'Upward' — describes movement in an upward direction, physically or figuratively (e.g. an improving trend).
entries.usage: aufwärts gehen (to go up/improve).

examples.sentence: Mit der Wirtschaft geht es wieder aufwärts.
examples.translation: The economy is improving again.
The arrow points upward.
Things would slowly improve.
The price is being revised upward.

entries.intro: 'Up (toward)' — describes upward motion away from the speaker, often combined with verbs as a separable prefix.
entries.usage: hinaufgehen (to go up), den Berg hinauf (up the mountain).

examples.translation: We walked up the mountain.

examples.sentence: Die Katze kletterte den Baum hinauf.
examples.translation: The cat climbed up the tree.

examples.sentence: Ich würde gern den Berg hinauf wandern.
examples.translation: I would like to hike up the mountain.

examples.sentence: Die Kisten werden die Treppe hinauf getragen.
examples.translation: The boxes are carried up the stairs.

entries.intro: The dative form of 'er' (he) or 'es' (it) — 'to him/to it'.
entries.usage: Ich gebe ihm das Buch (I give him the book).

examples.translation: I helped him.
I don't believe him.
I would like to help him.
He was offered the position.

entries.intro: 'Just/precisely' (temporal, 'just now') or a filler particle expressing resigned agreement ('that's just how it is').
entries.usage: Ich war eben da (I was just there); 'So ist es eben' (That's just how it is).

examples.sentence: Ich habe eben mit ihr telefoniert.
examples.translation: I just spoke with her on the phone.
I was just here a moment ago.
That would just be typical.
That is being taken care of right now.

entries.intro: 'Now' — the most direct and common word for the present moment.
entries.usage: Often starts a sentence, triggering inversion: 'Jetzt verstehe ich.'

examples.translation: I have to go now.
What are you doing now?
Now would be the right moment.
It is being decided now.

entries.intro: 'Now' — slightly more formal/literary than 'jetzt', and also used as a discourse filler meaning 'well then'.
entries.usage: 'Nun, was machen wir?' (Well then, what shall we do?).

examples.sentence: Nun ist es an der Zeit, zu gehen.
examples.translation: Now is the time to go.

examples.sentence: Nun, das ist eine gute Frage.
examples.translation: Well, that's a good question.
Now everything would be ready.

examples.sentence: Nun wird das Ergebnis bekannt gegeben.
examples.translation: Now the result is being announced.

entries.intro: The indefinite article 'a/an' for feminine nominative/accusative nouns — the feminine form of 'ein'.
entries.usage: eine Frau (a woman), eine Idee (an idea).

examples.translation: I have an idea.
She has a cat.
A break would be good now.
A new rule is being introduced.

entries.intro: The number 'one', used when counting on its own (not directly before a noun, where 'ein/eine' is used instead).
entries.usage: 'Eins, zwei, drei...' (One, two, three...) vs. 'ein Buch' (one book).

examples.translation: It's one o'clock.
I only need one of those.

examples.sentence: Es wäre schön, wenn wir alle eins wären.
examples.translation: It would be nice if we were all one/united.

examples.sentence: Es wird eins nach dem anderen erledigt.
examples.translation: It's done one after another.

entries.intro: Past participle of 'einkehren' — 'to stop in' (at an inn/restaurant while traveling) or, figuratively, 'to have settled in' (e.g. 'Ruhe ist eingekehrt' — calm has settled in).
entries.usage: einkehren, kehrte ein, ist eingekehrt (takes 'sein' as the perfect auxiliary — a motion/state-change verb).

examples.sentence: Nach dem Streit ist wieder Ruhe eingekehrt.
examples.translation: After the argument, calm has settled in again.

examples.sentence: Nach dem langen Streit ist endlich Frieden eingekehrt.
examples.translation: After the long argument, peace finally settled in.

examples.sentence: Ruhe wäre eingekehrt, wenn der Streit beendet worden wäre.
examples.translation: Calm would have settled in if the argument had ended.

examples.sentence: Es wird berichtet, dass Ruhe eingekehrt ist.
examples.translation: It is reported that calm has settled in.

entries.intro: The informal singular imperative of 'kommen' (to come) — 'Come!'. The infinitive 'kommen' (below) is the dictionary form; this is its command form used when speaking to one person you'd call 'du'.
entries.usage: komm! (to one person) vs. kommt! (to several people, informal) vs. kommen Sie! (formal).

examples.translation: Come here!
Please come on time.
You would surely like to come.

examples.sentence: Komm, das Zimmer wird gerade aufgeräumt.
examples.translation: Come, the room is being tidied up right now.

entries.intro: 'To come' — one of the most frequent and irregular German verbs, used for arrival, origin ('woher kommst du?' — where are you from?), and many idiomatic expressions.
entries.usage: kommen, kam, ist gekommen (takes 'sein' in the perfect tense). ich komme, du kommst, er/sie/es kommt.

examples.translation: When are you arriving?
Where are you from?
I would like to come earlier.

examples.sentence: Es wird erwartet, dass viele Gäste kommen.
examples.translation: It is expected that many guests will come.

entries.intro: 'Healthy' — describes physical wellbeing or, more broadly, something that is good for one's health (food, habits).
entries.usage: gesund sein (to be healthy), gesundes Essen (healthy food).

examples.sentence: Iss mehr Gemüse, das ist gesund.
examples.translation: Eat more vegetables, that's healthy.

examples.sentence: Er sieht heute nicht sehr gesund aus.
examples.translation: He doesn't look very healthy today.
That would be healthier for you.

examples.sentence: Gesundes Essen wird in der Kantine angeboten.
examples.translation: Healthy food is offered in the cafeteria.

entries.intro: 'Good/well' — one of the most common adjectives/adverbs in the language, used broadly for quality, skill, and wellbeing.
entries.usage: Irregular comparison: gut, besser, am besten (good, better, best).

examples.translation: The food tastes good.
I'm doing well.
That would be good for us.
Good work is always rewarded.

entries.intro: Has two common meanings: the informal second-person plural 'you (all)' as a subject pronoun, or the possessive 'her/their' before a noun.
entries.usage: As subject: 'Ihr seid spät' (You all are late). As possessive: 'ihr Buch' (her/their book).

examples.translation: You (all) are warmly welcome.
That is her/their car.
You (all) would be warmly welcome.
Her/their/your application is currently being processed.

entries.intro: The feminine/plural-inflected form of the possessive 'ihr' — 'her/their' before feminine singular or any plural noun.
entries.usage: ihre Tasche (her/their bag, fem.), ihre Kinder (her/their children, plural).

examples.translation: Her bag is red.
Her cat is very playful.

examples.sentence: Ihre Idee wäre eine gute Lösung.
examples.translation: Her/their idea would be a good solution.
Her/their questions will be answered shortly.

entries.intro: 'To what extent/in what way' — a somewhat formal question word probing how or how much something is true.
entries.usage: 'Inwiefern hat sich das geändert?' (In what way/to what extent has that changed?).

examples.translation: How does that concern me?

examples.sentence: Er erklärte, inwiefern sich die Regeln geändert hatten.
examples.translation: He explained to what extent the rules had changed.

examples.sentence: Ich würde gern wissen, inwiefern sich das ändern würde.
examples.translation: I would like to know to what extent that would change.

examples.sentence: Inwiefern die Regel angewendet wird, ist unklar.
examples.translation: To what extent the rule is applied is unclear.

entries.intro: 'Clear' — describes something easy to understand or see through (an idea, water, the sky). Also used alone as an informal 'sure!/of course!'.
entries.usage: klares Wasser (clear water); 'Klar!' (Sure!/Of course!).

examples.translation: Is that clear?
Sure, no problem!
That would be clear enough.
The rules are clearly explained.

entries.translation: gotten a share of (colloquial past participle)
entries.intro: Colloquial past participle of 'abkriegen' — 'to get a share of (something)' or, informally, 'to get hit/hurt'.
entries.usage: abkriegen, kriegte ab, hat abgekriegt — casual register, more common in speech than writing.

examples.sentence: Er hat bei der Prügelei etwas abgekriegt.
examples.translation: He got hurt a bit in the fight.

examples.sentence: Beim Umzug hat der Tisch einen Kratzer abgekriegt.
examples.translation: During the move, the table got a scratch.
He would have gotten almost nothing.

examples.sentence: Es wird erzählt, dass er dabei etwas abgekriegt hat.
examples.translation: It is said that he got hurt a bit in the process.

entries.intro: The simple past (first/third person singular) of 'bekommen' (to receive/get).
entries.usage: bekommen, bekam, hat bekommen. ich/er/sie/es bekam.

examples.translation: She received a letter.

examples.sentence: Sie bekam zum Geburtstag ein neues Fahrrad.
examples.translation: She got a new bike for her birthday.

examples.sentence: Er hätte einen Brief bekommen, wenn er die Adresse gehabt hätte.
examples.translation: He would have received a letter if he had had the address.

examples.sentence: Der Brief wurde ihm gestern zugestellt.
examples.translation: The letter was delivered to him yesterday.

entries.intro: 'Need/demand' — a formal noun describing a requirement or market demand for something.
entries.usage: der Bedarf (an + dative) — 'Bedarf an Fachkräften' (demand for skilled workers). No standard plural in most uses.

examples.sentence: Es besteht großer Bedarf an Wohnungen.
examples.translation: There is great demand for housing.

examples.sentence: Bei Bedarf können Sie mich jederzeit anrufen.
examples.translation: If needed, you can call me anytime.

examples.sentence: Es wäre Bedarf an mehr Personal vorhanden.
examples.translation: There would be a need for more staff.

examples.sentence: Der Bedarf wird jedes Jahr neu berechnet.
examples.translation: The demand is recalculated every year.

entries.intro: 'Need/necessity' — a more personal/emotional noun than 'Bedarf', often describing psychological or basic human needs.
entries.usage: das Bedürfnis, die Bedürfnisse (plural) — 'Grundbedürfnisse' (basic needs).

examples.sentence: Jeder Mensch hat das Bedürfnis nach Anerkennung.
examples.translation: Every person has the need for recognition.

examples.sentence: Ruhe ist für ihn ein wichtiges Bedürfnis.
examples.translation: Quiet is an important need for him.
The need would be understandable.
Her/their needs are taken seriously.

entries.intro: 'Lack/shortage' — describes an insufficient amount of something needed.
entries.usage: der Mangel an + dative — 'Mangel an Wasser' (lack of water). Plural: die Mängel (often 'defects' in a formal sense).

examples.sentence: Es gibt einen Mangel an Ärzten.
examples.translation: There is a shortage of doctors.

examples.sentence: Es herrscht ein Mangel an frischem Wasser.
examples.translation: There is a shortage of fresh water.

examples.sentence: Ein Mangel an Zeit wäre das größte Problem.
examples.translation: A lack of time would be the biggest problem.

examples.sentence: Der Mangel wird durch neue Lieferungen behoben.
examples.translation: The shortage is being resolved through new deliveries.

entries.intro: 'See' — the formal imperative of 'sehen', used almost exclusively as a cross-reference marker in texts ('siehe Seite 5' — see page 5), similar to English 'see' in citations.
entries.usage: Only used this way in written references, not as a spoken command (that would be 'sieh!' or 'schau!').

examples.translation: See chapter 3 for more details.
More information: see below.

examples.sentence: Man würde bei Unsicherheit sagen: siehe Anhang.
examples.translation: In case of uncertainty, one would say: see appendix.

examples.sentence: Im Text wird oft auf 'siehe oben' verwiesen.
examples.translation: The text often refers to 'see above'.

entries.intro: The simple past (first/third person singular) of 'tun' (to do) — 'did'.
entries.usage: tun, tat, hat getan. ich/er/sie/es tat.

examples.translation: He did his best.

examples.sentence: Sie tat so, als ob nichts passiert wäre.
examples.translation: She acted as if nothing had happened.
He would have done it just the same.

examples.sentence: Er tat, was getan werden musste.
examples.translation: He did what needed to be done.

entries.intro: The simple past plural of 'tun' (to do) — 'did' (we/they did). Inflected form of the same verb as 'tat' above.
entries.usage: wir/sie taten. Not to be confused with the capitalized noun 'Taten' (deeds), which is unrelated in form but shares the root.

examples.translation: They did what they could.

examples.sentence: Die Kinder taten, was man ihnen sagte.
examples.translation: The children did what they were told.

examples.sentence: Sie hätten mehr getan, wenn sie gekonnt hätten.
examples.translation: They would have done more if they could have.

examples.sentence: Es wurde bemerkt, was sie taten.
examples.translation: What they did was noticed.

entries.intro: 'Well-behaved/polite' — used almost exclusively to describe children or animals behaving well.
entries.usage: ein artiges Kind (a well-behaved child); 'Sei artig!' (Be good!).

examples.sentence: Sei artig, während ich weg bin.
examples.translation: Be good while I'm away.

examples.sentence: Der Hund war den ganzen Tag sehr artig.
examples.translation: The dog was very well-behaved all day.

examples.sentence: Die Kinder wären artiger, wenn sie müde wären.
examples.translation: The children would be better-behaved if they were tired.
Well-behaved conduct is always praised.

entries.intro: The neuter/inflected form of 'gut' (good) — appears before a neuter noun with no preceding article, or as a substantivized adjective ('etwas Gutes' — something good). Inflected form of the same word as 'gut' above.
entries.usage: gutes Essen (good food, neuter, no article); alles Gute (all the best).

examples.translation: I wish you all the best.

examples.sentence: Ich habe nur Gutes über dich gehört.
examples.translation: I've only heard good things about you.
Something good would be welcome now.

examples.sentence: Gutes wird oft mit Gutem vergolten.
examples.translation: Good is often repaid with good.
